title: U700's output capacitors C704-C707 are X5R parts rated to 85 C, not the X7R/X6S/X7S types TI lists.
what: C704-C707 are Murata GRM32ER61C476KE15L (47 uF 16 V X5R 1210, JLC C77101), rated -55 to +85 C. TI's recommended output capacitors for the TPSM63606 are X7R, X6S, X7S or X6T types. C704 and C705 sit next to U700. Capacitance is still enough: about 30 uF each at 5 V against TI's 30 uF total minimum.
consequence: If the area beside U700 runs above 85 C, the capacitors operate outside their rating and age faster. Failure would be gradual.
do: BOM-only change: fit an X7R 47 uF 1210 such as Murata GRM32ER71A476KE15L (C84494) on the same pads. Log the temperature beside U700 at bring-up.
source: TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B section 8.3.4 and Table 8-3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf ; https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C77101 ; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch C704 fields

title: A single fault in U700's feedback can put up to about 12 V on FE_5V, and nothing on FE_5V limits it.
what: FE_5V is set only by R700 (40.2 kOhm) and R701 (10 kOhm) on U700's FB pin, and U700's power-good, which enables all eight ports, also judges FB. FE_5V has 35 pads and no clamp, fuse or overvoltage cut-off. An open R700, a grounded FB or a failed module drives FE_5V towards the 12 V input; power-good then turns the ports off, but the eight TPS2553 switches (7 V maximum) are left holding that voltage. A wrong divider value (for example R700 about 55-115 kOhm) is worse: power-good stays high and every head gets 6.5-11.9 V, above the 6.5 V maximum of its U16 regulator.
consequence: One wrong 0603 resistor, one solder bridge or one module failure can overstress all eight port switches, or damage up to eight head stacks at once.
do: First power-up rule: power J4 with no cables, check FE_5V reads 4.9-5.15 V (at C704 pin 1, see HDMI-59) and TP701-TP708 read the same, and stop if not; repeat after any rework of U700, R700 or R701. In a later revision, add an overvoltage cut-off on FE_5V rated for the 12-15 V input.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B sections 7.5 and 8.3.9, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf ; TI TPS2553 SLVS841G section 6.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf

title: U602 drives the FT232H TDO pin while the FT232H, in its default UART mode, also drives that pin.
what: Level shifter U602 (TXU0304) drives HOST_TDO from a push-pull output (pin 5) straight into FT232H U501 pin 15 (ADBUS2), with no series resistor; only R509 (10 kOhm pull-up) is also on the net. U602 is enabled through DRIVE_ENABLE whenever SW601 is at ENABLE and the selected target's reference voltage is valid. In asynchronous UART mode, which the FT232H uses with a blank EEPROM such as the fitted U505, ADBUS2 is the RTS# output. The two outputs then fight until software switches the FT232H to its JTAG (MPSSE) mode.
consequence: Before the EEPROM is programmed, or whenever the FT232H sits in UART mode with a target enabled, both drivers short into each other. This stresses U602 and U501 beyond their ratings but is not an instant failure.
do: Keep SW601 at OFF until the U505 EEPROM is programmed for JTAG use. At the next layout change, add a 330 Ohm to 1 kOhm series resistor between U602 pin 5 and U501 pin 15.
where: Net HOST_TDO = U501.15, U602.5, R509.1; U602.8 OE = DRIVE_ENABLE (U605.1); U505 93LC56B EEPROM.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; TI TXU0304 SCES935A https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf ; FTDI UM232H-B data sheet pin table (ADBUS2 = RTS# in UART mode) https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/163/DS_UM232H-B-218263.pdf ; Linux ftdi_sio note on the UART default https://lore.kernel.org/all/20170719132327.2ddb8fbe@crub/T/

title: Several bypass capacitors of the USB-JTAG chips U501 (FT232H) and U602 sit 3-10 mm from their supply pins instead of right beside them.
what: U602 (TXU0304 level shifter): TI asks for a 0.1 uF capacitor on each supply pin, as close to the part as possible. The nearest capacitor to pin 1 (FTDI3V3) is C604 at 10.4 mm; the nearest to pin 14 (+1.8V) are C603 and C605 at 9.6 mm. +1.8V here is 0.2-0.3 mm track with no plane. U501 (FT232H USB-to-JTAG chip, top side): all of its regulator, PLL and PHY capacitors are on the bottom side. VREGIN pin 40 reaches C501 (100 nF) at 7.0 mm and C500 (4.7 uF) at 9.1 mm through about 8.2 mm of 0.2 mm track and a via, on a stub away from the FB502 bead that feeds the pin. VPLL pin 8 reaches C514/C513 at 5.4/6.3 mm on a separate stub, while its FB500 bead feeds the pin through 14.3 mm of 0.15 mm L3 track. VPHY pin 3 reaches C515/C516 at 2.9/4.2 mm. Opal Kelly's BRK8305 breakout, the source of this FT232H circuit, places the same capacitors on the top side 1.4-1.9 mm from the pins. Of the capacitors on U501's regulator, PLL and PHY pins, only C517 (VCORE) and C518 (VCCA) sit close, at 0.5 and 1.8 mm.
consequence: At U602, supply bounce when the outputs switch can add noise or false edges on the JTAG lines, including TCK; the risk is low at JTAG speeds. At U501, trace and via inductance ahead of any bypass adds supply noise to the USB High-Speed PHY and PLL, which can show up as unreliable High-Speed enumeration or bit errors on the built-in programmer that loads the XEM8310 and all eight Frontends. Both will most likely still work.
do: On the first board, check that the FT232H enumerates at High Speed (480 Mb/s) and run a long JTAG readback at the intended TCK. At the next layout change, add 100 nF capacitors right beside U602 pins 1 and 14, and move C500/C501, C513/C514 and C515/C516 next to U501 pins 40, 8 and 3 (top side as on BRK8305, or directly under the pins), routing each bead to its capacitor and then to the pin.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (pad positions and tracks); TI TXU0304 SCES935A section 12.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf ; FTDI DS_FT232H (pin functions), https://ftdichip.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/DS_FT232H.pdf ; Opal Kelly BRK8305 rev A03 layout (reference for the FT232H circuit)

title: The U801-U816 ESD-array pads do not follow TI's pattern: signal pads are wider and ground pads narrower.
what: U801-U816 are TPD4E02B04 arrays in a 1.0 x 2.5 mm 10-pad package at 0.5 mm pitch. All ten pads are 0.30 x 0.55 mm, so adjacent signal pads are 0.20 mm apart. TI's example uses 0.20 mm signal pads (0.30 mm gaps) and 0.40 mm ground pads (pins 3 and 8). The ground pads get about half TI's paste.
consequence: A solder bridge would short a cable signal line (recording, clock, command or SYNC) to its neighbour or to ground and is hard to see under the part. The added risk over TI's pattern is modest.
do: Ask JLC at file review whether the pads and the 0.22 x 0.47 mm paste openings are acceptable, or narrow the signal pads to 0.20-0.25 mm and widen pads 3/8 to 0.40 mm at the next layout change.
where: U801-U816 (footprint USON-10_2.5x1.0mm_P0.5mm), top side near x 75 mm.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (U801 pads); TI TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B pp.24-25, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf

title: JLC must confirm several order points in writing before production.
what: (1) In the JLC cart JLC adds its own 5 mm rails on the long edges (board becomes 167.65 x 124.1 mm), but the order note asks for rails on the left and right only: the bottom long edge is the gold-finger edge that needs the bevel, and J500 overhangs the top edge by about 1.2 mm. (2) The order form offers only 'Remove Mark' or a 2D barcode, not the order-number position marked on the bottom silk at (175, -131). (3) JLC's thickness tolerance for a 1.6 mm board is +/-10 %, 1.44-1.76 mm, while the note needs 1.44-1.70 mm at the fingers. (4) L3 has no copper pour (about 9 % copper) against about 93 % on L2, L4 and L5; the note invites JLC to propose balancing copper but sets no bow/twist limit. (5) The note asks for written acceptance of the 210 vias with 0.15 mm drills (about 10.6:1 in the 1.594 mm board). These vias (0.25 mm pad) and the 142 vias with 0.20 mm drills (0.30 mm pad) have a 0.05 mm annular ring, JLC's minimum; JLC prefers the pad 0.15 mm larger than the hole. The note does not mention the rings.
consequence: Rails on the long edges conflict with the finger bevel and the overhanging USB-C connector. A board thicker than 1.70 mm at the fingers may not seat in the slot. Uneven copper can bow the card. Rings at the minimum leave no margin for drill wander in the deep 0.15 mm holes. Without answers these points are settled by JLC, not by the design.
do: At file review, get JLC to confirm in writing: rails on the left and right edges only, the order-number position, 1.44-1.70 mm at the fingers, any L3 balancing copper (kept 1.0 mm from pairs) with a bow/twist limit, the 0.15 mm drills, and the 0.05 mm rings on the 0.15/0.25 mm and 0.20/0.30 mm vias.
where: Board outline (167.65 x 114.10 mm); J6 finger edge y 162.05; J500 at the top edge; L3 (In2.Cu); the 352 smallest vias (210 x 0.15/0.25 mm, 142 x 0.20/0.30 mm); order note sections PCB 1, 2, 4, 5, Silkscreen and Assembly 1.
source: ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V39.md; JLC test cart of 16 Nov 2026 (HDMI V38 order record); JLCPCB capabilities https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (zones, vias)

title: The USB-JTAG programmer's notes sit in one box far from the nine circuits they explain, instead of one box beside each circuit.
what: The schematic's USB-to-JTAG section has a single note box at (1073, 280)-(1288, 455), to the right of all its parts. Its Function and Source/changes items cover nine separately cited sub-circuits: USB-C input, FT232H and EEPROM, translator, rail bypass, rotary selector, OFF/ENABLE switch, voltage window, delay and XEM target switch. Most parts sit far from the nearest edge of the box: U602 115 mm, U501 335 mm, U610 460 mm, U605 562 mm, SW600/SW601 658 mm, U603 723 mm, C601 789 mm, C608 840 mm; only R601-R603 and C605 beside U602 are closer, at 60-85 mm. The sub-circuits already have their own headings (TARGET SELECTION, XEM JTAG RAIL BYPASS, TARGET VOLTAGE CHECK AND ENABLE, 1.8 V JTAG TRANSLATOR, XEM JTAG TARGET) but no box. Each HDMI port on the same page has its own boxes beside its parts. The workspace schematic rule asks for each circuit's two items to be in a box right beside it, and it says a detached notes column does not count. The shared box was an earlier deliberate change, but no record accepts it as an exception.
consequence: A reader cannot tie each citation and list of changes to its circuit. For example, the TPS3700 window thresholds (U603) and the TPS3808 delay (U605) are explained about 700 mm from those parts. No electrical effect.
do: At the next schematic edit, split the box into one two-item box (function; source and changes with its citation) beside each sub-circuit: USB-C/ESD, FT232H/EEPROM/crystal, TXU0304 translator, SW600/SW601 selection, U603/U605 window and delay, and U610/R629 with the rail bypass C601/C603. Spread the drawing where needed, check that no box overlaps a symbol, wire or label, and keep the netlist unchanged.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch (note box, sub-circuit headings and symbol positions); workspace rule 'References in schematics' (two items in a visible box beside each circuit)

title: Some part fields name a different part from the one JLC fits, and this board keeps its JLC numbers in a 'JLCPCB' field instead of 'LCSC'.
what: (1) The C6 BOM line reads 'TMK105BJ104KV-F, C6, C77014', and the schematic gives the same Taiyo Yuden part number. JLC C77014 is Murata GRM155R71E104KE14D, an equivalent 100 nF 25 V 0402 capacitor (X7R instead of X5R). (2) The Datasheet links of U700's feedback and timing resistors point to other makers' parts. R700 (40.2 kOhm) links JLC C308258 (ROHM MCR03EZPFX4022) but is ordered as C137723 (Yageo RC0603FR-0740K2L). R702 (13 kOhm) links C4083262 (Panasonic ERJ-H3EF1302V) but is ordered as C22797 (UNI-ROYAL 0603WAF1302T5E). Values and packages match. (3) All 270 fitted parts carry their JLC C-number (the JLC/LCSC part number) in a field named 'JLCPCB'. The Frontend, FPGA-LDO and ASIC boards use 'LCSC', as the project's parts rule asks. The numbers themselves are complete and match the order BOM.
consequence: JLC places the right parts, but the BOM text, the datasheet links and the schematic do not say so. This can draw a query at order review and confuses traceability. A BOM rebuilt from the schematic, or the project's board-check script, which reads an 'LCSC' field, finds no C-numbers on this board and so skips the board-to-BOM comparison.
do: In one text-only field pass (no netlist or copper change): change C6's value and part number to GRM155R71E104KE14D (or mark it as a substitute) in the schematic and BOM; point the R700 and R702 Datasheet fields at the fitted parts (https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C137723 and https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C22797, or the makers' data sheets); copy the 'JLCPCB' field to an 'LCSC' field on all 270 parts.
where: C6 (+VDCIN bypass), order BOM line 'TMK105BJ104KV-F,C6,BRK_C6,C77014'; R700 (U700 FB, 40.2 kOhm), R702 (U700 RT, 13 kOhm); 'JLCPCB' field on all 270 fitted symbols and footprints.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39_BOM.csv; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch (C6, R700, R702 and part-number fields); https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C77014 ; https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C308258 ; https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C4083262 ; workspace rule 'JLC parts only' (C-number in the LCSC field)

title: Only two of the four XEM8310 standoff holes exist, so two module corners are held only by the connectors, and the schematic note disagrees about which holes exist.
what: Opal Kelly's mating drawing calls for four 3.20 mm holes for M3 standoffs, one near each corner of the 100 x 70 mm module. The board has only MH3 and MH2, on one diagonal. Tracks pass within 0.2-0.6 mm of the other two sites (B86 pairs on L1; MGT and B64 nets on L3 and L6), so the holes cannot be added without rerouting. The schematic's XEM8310 note box contradicts itself. Its Function item says the module is held by its connectors and M3 standoffs at MH2/MH3, with MH1/MH4 routed over, which matches the board. Its Source/changes item still says the module is held at MH1/MH2 only, and then that MH1/MH2 were removed too and only MC1-MC3 hold it.
consequence: Pressing on the module, plugging its USB-C, or vibration loads the connector solder joints at the free corners, which can crack them over time. A reader of the schematic may conclude there are no standoff holes at all, or look for MH1.
do: Put a glued nylon spacer or bumper under the two free corners. Add the holes if the area is ever rerouted. Rewrite the note's Source/changes text to the current state: MH2 and MH3 fitted; MH1 and MH4 left out because tracks run over those sites.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Mating Board Diagram, https://docs.opalkelly.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/XEM8310-Mating-Board-Diagram-1.pdf ; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (holes and tracks); HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch (XEM8310 note box)

title: The J920 test-hole row puts 12 V between two ground holes and unlike XEM8310 rails only 0.71 mm apart.
what: The nine test holes have 2.54 mm pads on a 3.25 mm pitch, leaving 0.71 mm of gap. +VDCIN (12 V, unfused) sits between two DGND holes. +1.2V_DDR sits next to VIO1, VIO1 next to +1.8V, +3.3V next to VIO3, and VIO3 next to VIO2.
consequence: A slipping probe can short the 12 V adapter to ground or force a higher rail onto a lower XEM8310 rail, which can damage the module's DDR4 or VIO regulators.
do: Probe J920 only with sprung hook clips or with the board unpowered. In a later revision, put ground holes between rails or space the holes further apart.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (J920 pads); netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; Opal Kelly XEM8310 Device Settings, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/device-settings/

title: The back silkscreen says the red LEDs D701-D708 mean 'port 5 V on', but they light only when a port switch reports a fault.
what: The bottom legend reads 'D701-D708 red LED = port 5 V on' and the top text says 'switched per port, LED on back'. Each LED runs from FE_5V through R721-R728 (3.3 kOhm) into the FAULT pin (pin 4) of its TPS2553 switch U701-U708. FAULT is an open-drain output that goes low only in over-current, over-temperature or reverse voltage. A healthy port has a dark LED.
consequence: At bring-up a healthy board shows eight dark LEDs, which the legend calls 'off', and a port stuck in current limit lights its LED, which the legend calls 'on'. Debugging starts in the wrong place.
do: Change the back legend to 'D701-D708 red = port FAULT (over-current / over-temperature); off = normal' and the front text to 'FAULT LED on back', then regenerate the silkscreen Gerbers.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (silk texts); netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; TI TPS2553 SLVS841G Table 5-1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf

title: The board does not show which position the JTAG selector SW600 or the enable switch SW601 is in.
what: SW600 is a 9-position rotary switch with a plain flatted shaft. The silk says 'JTAG TARGET: 0 = XEM, 1-8 = P1-P8', but there is no dial, index or position number around it, only two outline lines and a corner mark. SW601 is a slide switch with a single 'OFF/ENABLE' label below it and no mark showing which end is OFF.
consequence: All eight Frontends carry the same FPGA, so Vivado cannot tell which port is selected; an image can go to the wrong head. Rules such as 'keep SW601 at OFF' cannot be followed from the board alone.
do: Add silk ticks numbered 0-8 at the SW600 detents (or fit a knob with a pointer) and print OFF and ENABLE at the two ends of SW601. Confirm the SW601 direction with a meter on the first board: ENABLE connects MASTER (SW601 pin 6) to +3.3V.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (SW600/SW601 footprint silk); Alps SRBQ catalog https://tech.alpsalpine.com/cms.media/product_catalog_sw_04_srbq_en_aaa09fb719.pdf

title: Header J910 mixes 1.8 V bank-64 holes with VIO2 bank-84 holes, and the silk does not give each bank's voltage.
what: J910 brings out bank 64 I/O (high-performance bank, 1.8 V maximum, powered by VIO1) beside bank 84 I/O (up to 3.3 V, powered by VIO2), plus VIO2, VREF1, VBATT and VIO1. The back silk names each hole's bank but not its voltage.
consequence: A bench jumper from VIO2 at 3.3 V to a bank-64 hole would overdrive that bank.
do: Keep a header map that gives bank 64 = VIO1 (up to 1.8 V) and bank 84 = VIO2; add the voltages to the silk in a later revision.
where: J910: pins 1-7, 10, 20 bank 64; 8 VREF1; 17 VIO2; 27 VBATT; 30 VIO1; the rest bank 84.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; Opal Kelly XEM8310 Expansion Connectors, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/expansion-connectors/

title: Each port's current limit leaves little margin over the high-case head load, and pin 19 carries it alone.
what: Each port switch (TPS2553, R711-R718 = 37.4 kOhm) limits at 630-771 mA. The recorded high-case head load is 0.55 A at the 5 V pin, and the head's buck regulator draws more current as cable resistance lowers its input voltage. The stimulation supply on the FPGA-LDO board ramps for about 8 ms at start-up and adds roughly 0.1-0.3 A at 5 V while it does. All of this flows through the single pin-19 contact, which Molex rates 0.8 A at 25 C and 0.3 A per contact with all 19 contacts powered at 55 C.
consequence: With a high-load head, the port may sit in current limit, mainly during start-up, so the head browns out or restarts. Pin 19 at both cable ends may run warmer than Molex has qualified.
do: On the first stack, log the port current from cable insertion to 100 ms and in steady recording and stimulation, measure the cable's pin-19 loop resistance, and check pin-19 temperature after 30 min at the highest load.
where: U701-U708 pin 5 with R711-R718; PORT1_5V-PORT8_5V to J610-J617 pin 19; Frontend J3.19 VIN_5V to U16.
source: TI TPS2553 SLVS841G eq. 1-3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf ; Molex PS-46765-003 secs. 4.2 and 5.1 (distributor copy https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/026/DOC027026286.pdf); ADI LT3582 data sheet p.14, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf

title: All eight ports switch together on U700's power-good; the FPGA cannot switch, reset or monitor a port.
what: PORT_ENABLE connects only U700 pin 13 (PG), R703 and the eight switch EN pins. The switch FAULT outputs drive only the bottom-side LEDs. No XEM pin or header reads them or drives the enables.
consequence: A hung head can only be power-cycled by pulling its cable or the 12 V input, and one dip on FE_5V restarts all eight heads at once.
do: Nothing for this build. In a later revision, route the port enables and a combined FAULT signal to spare XEM pins.
where: Net PORT_ENABLE = U700.13, R703.1, U701-U708 pin 3; FAULT U701-U708 pin 4 to D701-D708.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch

title: A shorted or very low R711-R718 silently removes that port's current limit.
what: Each port's limit is set only by its ILIM resistor (37.4 kOhm). TI specifies the limit only for 15-232 kOhm; at 15 kOhm it is already 1.6-1.8 A. A bridged or wrong low-value resistor shows no symptom in normal use.
consequence: A later short in that port's cable or head then pushes several amps through pin 19 and the thin cable wire, or pulls U700 into its limit so all eight heads restart repeatedly.
do: Before first power, measure 36-39 kOhm from each U701-U708 pin 5 to ground.
where: U701-U708 pin 5 (ILIM) to R711-R718 pin 2; R71x pin 1 to DGND (bottom side).
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; TI TPS2553 SLVS841G sections 6.3 and 8.5.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf

title: The right-hand U700 capacitors and the feedback resistor R701 reach the module's ground only through vias to L2.
what: TI's layout ties the ground ends of the input and output capacitors to the module's PGND pads on top-side copper. On the left side C700/C702 and C704/C706 do this (ground pads at x 123.275 in the centre PGND copper). On the right side C701/C703 and C705/C707 have their ground pads at x 128.175 on two separate top-side islands that reach PGND only through vias to the L2 plane. The lower feedback resistor R701 (10 kOhm) is grounded the same way. A single 0.25 mm L1 track runs from its pad 1 at (127.97, 62.40) into the 'U700 PGND output east' island that also carries the C705/C707 ground pads, and an FE_5V pour cuts that island off from the PGND copper under the module. TI asks for this resistor to go to AGND (pins 6 and 11), which is tied correctly to PGND pin 19 here.
consequence: A slightly larger switching loop on the right side and somewhat more noise, including a few millivolts on U700's feedback reference through R701's ground. The solid L2 plane, the module's internal input capacitors and the 22 pF feed-forward capacitor C708 limit the effect.
do: Nothing for this build. If the U700 area is reworked, mirror the four right-hand capacitors so their ground pads join the centre PGND copper, and run R701's ground end to the AGND pin 11 / PGND pin 19 track under the module.
where: C701, C703, C705, C707; R701 pad 1 (127.97, 62.40); L1 zones 'U700 PGND input east' and 'U700 PGND output east'.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (pads, tracks and zones); TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B Table 6-1 (FB pin) and section 11.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf

title: Frontend JTAG through the cable is estimated to work only up to about 6 MHz TCK, below Vivado's common 15 MHz default.
what: The TDO answer must return within half a TCK period. The loop adds U602 both ways (19 + 14 ns), the cable both ways, the FPGA clock-to-TDO time (7 ns), a heavily loaded 225 mm TDO trunk and the FT232H setup time (11 ns). With the 0.9 m cable this is about 80 ns, so TCK is limited to about 6 MHz.
consequence: At 15 MHz, scans or programming of a head may fail intermittently, which looks like a cable or board fault.
do: Start Frontend JTAG at 3-6 MHz in hw_server and step up while checking IDCODE reads; record the working limit.
where: JTAG_TCK_1V8 / JTAG_TDO_1V8 trunks from U602 to U610-U618; R640-R671; J610-J617 pins 17/18.
source: TI TXU0304 SCES935A section 7.11, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf ; AMD DS181 boundary-scan timing; AMD UG908 JTAG clock frequency; cable delay about 5 ns/m (engineering judgement)

title: Y500's load capacitors may pull the FT232H clock 20-55 ppm fast, beyond FTDI's +/-30 ppm.
what: Y500 (SJK 7U12000E18UCG) is specified for an 18 pF load, but two 18 pF capacitors plus pin and trace capacitance give it only about 11-14 pF. The estimated pull is 20-55 ppm fast, before the crystal's own tolerance. FTDI asks for 12 MHz within +/-30 ppm. The same values are on Opal Kelly's BRK8305 and USB is expected to work.
consequence: The FT232H runs outside its stated clock tolerance and USB has less margin. Enumeration will most likely still work.
do: Check USB enumeration on the first boards. If it is unreliable, fit 27 pF C0G 0402 for C503/C504 on the same pads.
where: Y500 on U501 OSCI/OSCO; C503, C504 (KEMET C0402C180J5GACTU, 18 pF).
source: SJK 7U12000E18UCG spec (LCSC copy), https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/5264ef3486a068e24cbf9f4599b78983.pdf?productCode=C524717 ; FTDI DS_FT232H section 6.3, https://ftdichip.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/DS_FT232H.pdf

title: The PCIe fingers are thin immersion gold (ENIG), not the hard gold card-edge contacts normally use.
what: JLC makes gold fingers only with ENIG; the test cart is set to ENIG 1 u" (about 0.025 um of gold over nickel). Card-edge contacts are normally hard electroplated gold, which wears much more slowly.
consequence: The fingers wear after repeated insertions. This is acceptable for a card that stays in its adapter.
do: Keep the card in its adapter and limit insertions.
where: J6 fingers A1-A49 and B1-B49.
source: JLCPCB gold fingers, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers ; JLC test cart of 16 Nov 2026 (finish ENIG 1 u")

title: The Micro-HDMI mouths sit flush with the left board edge, not 0.70 mm beyond it as Molex draws.
what: Molex's layout puts the board edge 1.70 mm in front of the front shell-slot centre, so the receptacle face stands 0.70 mm beyond the edge. Here the slot centres are at x 67.08 and the edge at x 64.676, so the board runs 0.70 mm further and the eight mouths are flush.
consequence: If the routed edge comes out slightly proud, a thick plug overmold may not seat fully or latch.
do: Check that the chosen cable seats and latches on every port of the first board.
where: Left Edge.Cuts at x 64.676; J610-J617 shell slots at x 67.08 and 70.44.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (J610 pads, outline); Molex SD-46765-001 sheets 2 and 5 (LCSC copy), https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/9c9e510abc6d42a6dc46064567ae3921.pdf?productCode=C563878

title: The 28 polarized bottom-side parts must be checked in JLC's placement preview.
what: JLC does not publish how it reads angles for bottom-side parts. Under the placement file's convention all 28 polarized bottom parts land correctly, but under other readings 10 or 18 of them would be turned 180 degrees. The order note has a pin-1 table for every one, and the cart has 'Confirm parts placement' on.
consequence: If the preview is approved without checking, port-fault LEDs or the port and JTAG switches could be fitted reversed.
do: Approve JLC's placement preview only after each of the 28 parts shows pin 1 or the cathode where the pin-1 table says.
where: Bottom side: D701-D708, U602, U603, U605, U610-U618, U701-U708; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39_CPL.csv.
source: ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V39.md pin-1 table; JLCPCB pick-and-place help, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pick-place-file-for-pcb-assembly

title: Printed paste fills only about a quarter of each Micro-HDMI shell slot, so the 32 shell joints rely on the top fillet.
what: Each shell slot (0.65 x 1.70 mm, plated) gets the 2.55 x 1.50 mm pad print plus a 2.55 x 1.05 mm overprint, about 6 mm2 of paste. With a 0.10-0.12 mm stencil that fills only about 20-25 % of the slot. The tabs reach only 0.4-0.7 mm into the 1.59 mm board.
consequence: Shell joints are weaker than a filled through-hole joint; a connector may loosen under repeated cable force or a side pull.
do: Inspect for a full top fillet on all 32 tabs (the order note asks for hand touch-up) and pull-test one connector on the first boards.
where: J610-J617 SH pads (32), top paste.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (J610 pads and F.Paste); Molex SD-46765-001 sheet 2 (LCSC copy), https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/9c9e510abc6d42a6dc46064567ae3921.pdf?productCode=C563878

title: C5's lands are smaller than Panasonic's recommended pattern for this 8 x 10.2 mm can.
what: C5 (EEE-FK1E221GP, size F) has 3.6 x 1.65 mm lands with a 3.05 mm gap. Panasonic recommends 4.0 x 2.0 mm lands with a 3.1 mm gap, so the land area is about 26 % smaller.
consequence: Slightly weaker joints on the board's tallest surface-mount part, with more risk of cracking if the card is flexed or dropped.
do: Inspect C5's fillets on the first boards; enlarge the lands at the next layout change.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (C5 pads); Panasonic land pattern table, https://industrial.panasonic.cn/content/data/CP/PDF/Alumi/AL_landP_e.pdf

title: 125 silkscreen labels are 0.8 mm tall, below JLC's 1.0 mm minimum text height.
what: The 107 back-side labels that name the J900-J911 header pins and their FPGA pairs, and the 18 test-pad names (16 on the back, 2 on top), are 0.8 mm tall with 0.15 mm strokes. JLC states 1.0 mm minimum text height. All other silk text is 1.0 mm or larger.
consequence: The labels may print blurred, making it easier to wire the wrong header pin or probe the wrong pad at bring-up. No electrical effect.
do: Keep a printed header map and the probe map with the board and check legibility on the first boards.
where: Bottom silk near J900-J902 and J910/J911; test-pad names at TP720-TP739 (TP727 and TP731 have none).
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (silk texts); JLCPCB capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities

title: U700 has less heat-spreading copper than TI's test boards, so its temperature at high load must be measured.
what: U700 (TPSM63606, 12 V to 5 V, 6 A) sheds heat through 12 vias (0.3 mm) into 15 um inner planes and small top-side ground areas (35.6, 15.3 and 15.1 mm2); the board has 35 um outer copper, while TI recommends 2 oz (70 um) and at least 1 oz. TI's thermal figures come from 2 oz boards (22.6-33.1 C/W). With about 33 C/W, the junction reaches about 97-104 C at the 4.4 A high case in 50 C air, and its 125 C limit at about 5.3-5.65 A.
consequence: Normal use should stay below 125 C. With all ports near their current limit in warm air, U700 can run past its rating or thermally limit and drop all eight ports.
do: At bring-up, load FE_5V to the measured worst case in the intended enclosure and log U700's top temperature (the junction is about 1 C above it). Add airflow or a heat sink if it passes about 100 C.
where: U700 at (124.0, 60.0), top side; zones 'U700 PGND centre / input east / output east' (L1) and 'U700 thermal L6'.
source: TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B sections 7.4 and 11.1 and Fig. 7-13, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf ; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (zones, vias, stack-up)

title: The PC-end enclosure's inside air temperature is unknown, and SW600 (60 C) and the XEM8310 (70 C) set its limit.
what: The enclosure is closed, has no fan and holds the board, the XEM8310 and the Thunderbolt adapter, about 14-28 W of heat. A rough estimate puts the inside air 15-49 C above the room; nothing is measured. The lowest-rated parts are SW600 (Alps SRBQ490100, -10 to +60 C) and the XEM8310 module (0 to +70 C), both below the upper estimate.
consequence: A warm box puts SW600 and the XEM8310 outside their ratings and lowers the current U700 can deliver.
do: Run the board and XEM8310 in the box with a dummy FE_5V load and log box air, SW600 and U700 temperature; use 60 C at SW600 and 70 C beside the XEM8310 as pass limits, or add vents or a fan.
where: SW600 at (196.0, 56.5); XEM8310 on MC1-MC3; U700; PC-end enclosure.
source: Alps SRBQ490100 product page, https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/SRBQ490100/ ; Opal Kelly XEM8310 Specifications, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/specifications/

title: The USB-C connector J500 and the rotary switch SW600 have simplified 3D shapes, not the makers' models.
what: J500 uses a project-made 'USB4110 dimensioned shell envelope' and SW600 an 'ALPS SRBQ490100 nominal proxy'. Their key heights match the makers' figures: J500's top is at 3.26 mm, as in GCT's USB4110 drawing, and SW600's shaft tip is 9.8 mm above the board, as Alps gives. The detailed shapes (the USB-C mouth and shell, the switch body and its flatted shaft) are simplified.
consequence: Enclosure and print-model checks built from the board's 3D data are approximate around the USB-C opening and the switch shaft hole. No effect on the board or its assembly.
do: Replace both with the makers' STEP files (GCT USB4110, Alps SRBQ490100) before the next enclosure or print-model rebuild, and recheck the USB-C opening and the shaft hole.
where: J500 (USB-C, top edge) and SW600 at (196.0, 56.5); their 3D model links in HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (footprint 3D model links and STEP product names); Alps SRBQ490100 product page, https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/SRBQ490100/ ; GCT USB4110 drawing

title: The 12 V input J4 has no fuse, reverse-polarity or overvoltage protection, the same as Opal Kelly's BRK8310.
what: J4 connects straight to +VDCIN, which feeds the XEM8310 (7.5-15 V) through MC2 and the 5 V module U700. The XEM8310's own barrel jack is on the same net. +VDCIN has 16 pads and none is a fuse, diode, TVS or blocking FET.
consequence: A 19-24 V or centre-negative adapter can destroy the XEM8310 and reverse-bias C5; two adapters in both jacks back-feed each other.
do: Use one labelled 12 V centre-positive adapter rated above 5 A, and never both jacks. Consider a fuse, TVS and reverse-blocking FET in a later revision.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; Opal Kelly Powering the XEM8310, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/powering-the-xem8310/

title: Five cable pins on each port (1, 2, 15, 17, 18) rely only on the analog switch's own 6 kV ESD rating.
what: The TPD4E02B04 arrays protect the four shielded pairs of each port (+/-12 kV contact). Pin 1 (VREF) goes straight to a TS3A27518E switch input, and the JTAG pins 2, 15, 17 and 18 reach it through 100 Ohm resistors. These five pins rely on the switch's +/-6 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact rating.
consequence: A discharge above 6 kV on one of these pins can damage that port's switch and lose JTAG or VREF sensing to that head. Data paths are not affected.
do: Handle cables with ESD care. Consider a low-capacitance array on these pins in a later revision.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; TI TS3A27518E SCDS260F p.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ts3a27518e.pdf ; TI TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf

title: The XEM8310 ships with VIO1 at 1.0 V, too low for the port LVDS outputs and the U2/U6/Q1 path.
what: VIO1 powers XEM bank 64, which drives every port's clock, command and SYNC, and also feeds VREF1 of the PCA9306 translators U2/U6 and the gate of Q1. Opal Kelly's default is 1.0 V, and a new setting needs a power cycle. The board has a silk reminder 'VIO1 = 1.8 V' but cannot enforce it.
consequence: With the factory setting the heads get no valid clock or commands, and the PCIe SMBus/WAKE path may stay off. Nothing is damaged, but it is easy to misdiagnose.
do: First bring-up step: set VIO1 to 1.8 V in the XEM8310 device settings, power-cycle, and measure VIO1 at J920 pin 2 before connecting heads.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Device Settings, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/device-settings/ ; TI PCA9306, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/pca9306.pdf

title: With SW601 at ENABLE and SW600 at 0, a running Vivado Hardware Manager can disturb the XEM8310's boot from flash.
what: Opal Kelly warns that an active JTAG connection can disturb the XEM8310's power-on load from flash. On this board the JTAG adapter is built in: U610 joins the XEM JTAG pins to the shared lines when SW600 is at 0 and SW601 at ENABLE, and U602 starts driving them 12-28 ms after the module's rails come up, long before the boot ends.
consequence: Power cycles with Vivado connected can leave the XEM unconfigured: no PCIe endpoint and no port clocks or commands.
do: Power up with SW601 at OFF; use SW601 ENABLE with SW600 at 0 only to program or debug the XEM, and close the Hardware Manager before power-cycling.
where: MC2.71/72/74/76 - U610 (EN = SEL_0) - JTAG_*_1V8 - U602 (OE = DRIVE_ENABLE from U605, CT open) - U501.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Flash Memory, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/flash-memory/ ; AMD UG908 'Configuration Failures in Master Mode', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Configuration-Failures-in-Master-Mode ; TI TPS3808 SBVS050, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3808.pdf

title: Test point TP700 (FE_5V) is mostly under the XEM8310; C704 or C706 pin 1 is a reachable FE_5V probe point.
what: TP700 is a 1.5 mm round pad at (134.25, 65.50). The XEM8310 outline, placed from Opal Kelly's mating drawing by the MH2/MH3 holes and the MC1-MC3 pegs, covers x 132.33-232.33 and y 65.15-135.15 mm. Its edge crosses the pad 0.35 mm from the centre, so 1.38 of the 1.77 mm2 (78 %) lies under the module and only a 0.40 mm sliver on the U700 side stays clear. Its 'FE 5V' label at (138.2, 65.5) is fully under the module.
consequence: With the XEM8310 fitted, FE_5V cannot be probed reliably at TP700, which is the point the first-power check needs.
do: Probe FE_5V at C704 pin 1 (120.33, 65.0) or C706 pin 1 (120.33, 68.4): 1.15 x 2.7 mm top-side pads about 12 mm clear of the module. R703 pin 2 (130.05, 57.52) also works; TP709 (DGND, 133.5, 57.0) is a clear ground reference. Move TP700 off the module area at the next layout change.
where: TP700 (FE_5V), C704/C706 pin 1, R703 pin 2, TP709; XEM8310 corner near MH3.
source: HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_pcb (TP700, MH2, MH3, MC1-MC3 pegs); Opal Kelly XEM8310 Mating Board Diagram, https://docs.opalkelly.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/XEM8310-Mating-Board-Diagram-1.pdf

title: On ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 the head's separate SYNC input is left floating, and the SYNC constraint comment and schematic texts are out of date.
what: Pins 12/14 are driven only on ports 3-6; on J610, J611, J616 and J617 they are unconnected. At the head, /CABLE_SYNC_P/N go to FPGA balls B9/A9 (LVDS input) with only R64 (100 Ohm) and an ESD part, so the receiver has no defined idle level. One Frontend image serves every port. The comment in fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc still says the Frontend routes 12/14 to its transceiver and warns not to drive sync_out. The HDMI schematic still shows eight free texts 'HDMIx_SYNC_P/N (ESD only, not routed to the XEM)' on these four ports. They sit between J61x pins 12/14 and the unused IO pins of U809, U810, U815 and U816, with no wire between them. Those connector pins carry no-connect flags, and the port boxes beside them correctly say '12/14 not connected'.
consequence: If the head firmware trusts pins 12/14, heads on ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 can see false SYNC events. The leftover schematic texts suggest these pins are ESD-protected or wired, which they are not.
do: Have the Frontend firmware use the SYNC folded into pins 9/11 by default, and use 12/14 only when it sees valid activity. Update the comment in fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc. Delete the eight schematic texts or reword them to 'J61x 12/14 not connected; U8xx IO1/IO2 unused'.
where: J610/J611/J616/J617 pins 12/14 (unconnected); J612-J615 pins 12/14 from MC1 through U811-U814; Frontend /CABLE_SYNC_P/N = J3.12/14, R64, U1 B9/A9, U18. Schematic texts at x 113.03 and 398.78 (y 928.37/933.45) and at x 684.53 and 970.28 (y 1144.27/1149.35).
source: Netlists from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch and the Frontend schematic V57; Frontend_V57_pins_V4.xdc lines 153-154; fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc lines 3-4; HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch (free texts on ports 1, 2, 7 and 8)

title: WAKE#, SMDAT and SMCLK are not constrained, so Vivado's default pull-down can hold the PCIe WAKE# line low.
what: The three PCIe sideband lines reach XEM bank 64 through 0 Ohm resistors R9-R11, and the pin file leaves them unconstrained on purpose, so Vivado applies its default pull-down to unused pins. WAKE# has only a 100 kOhm pull-up (R25, about 18 uA at 1.8 V), so the pull-down can hold it low, and U6 passes that low to the slot. SMCLK and SMDAT have 4.75 kOhm pull-ups and are not affected.
consequence: A host may see a constant wake request on J6 B11.
do: Constrain the three pins as LVCMOS18 inputs with no pull, or set BITSTREAM.CONFIG.UNUSEDPIN to Pullnone, in the XEM build.
where: /PCIE_WAKE_B_VIO = R9, R25, TP15, U6.3; /PCIE_WAKE_B_3V3 = J6.B11, TP16, U6.6; R10/R11 SMDAT/SMCLK; fit_pins_V34.xdc lines 75-78.
source: Netlist from HDMI_Extension_Board_V39.kicad_sch; AMD UG908 bitstream settings, https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Artix-Virtex-and-Kintex-UltraScale-Bitstream-Settings

title: A standard XEM8310 flash boot takes about 0.3-0.5 s, so the PCIe endpoint can miss the host's first link training.
what: At power-up the XEM8310 loads its whole 123.4 Mb XCAU25P bitstream from flash: about 0.26-0.49 s with Opal Kelly's quad-SPI flash settings, against the roughly 100 ms PCIe allows after slot power. The board's three XEM constraint files do not yet set those flash settings; with Vivado's defaults the load would take about 46 s. In the PC-end enclosure the Thunderbolt adapter and the XEM8310 start from the same 12 V, and whether the adapter or the Mac retries the link later is not documented. On the board, U4 holds the XEM's PERST# input in reset until the slot side is powered.
consequence: The Mac may show no XEM8310 PCIe device after power-up, sometimes or every time, which looks like a cable or driver fault.
do: Add Opal Kelly's flash-boot settings to a separate flash-build XDC. Either use a Tandem PROM build or power the board first and plug the Thunderbolt cable in afterwards; check on the bench whether the Mac finds the endpoint with the cable left in.
where: XEM8310 FPGA and flash; J6 PCIe x4; PERST# path J6.A11 - U4 - R7 - MC3.78; firmware files fit_pins_V34.xdc, fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc, header_pins_V34.xdc (no CONFIG or SPI settings).
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Flash Memory, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/flash-memory/ ; AMD PG213 Tandem Configuration, https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Tandem-Configuration ; AMD UG570 Table 1, https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug570-ultrascale-configuration/Device-Resources-and-Configuration-Bitstream-Lengths
